proof: A Go file and a markdown file in one repository: retrieval indexes both as text and the symbol query makes no claim about the Go file; the Context Inspector carries the language state per entry (language, tier, structural, needs_opt_in, degradation); the Go edit is refused with the language named until the user opts the task in with AllowUnsupportedLanguage, and the change that follows carries language=go and unsupported_language=true on the canonical FileChanged event while the markdown change carries language=markdown and false. A repository with no runner of ours gets evidence only from .modbit/verification.json, and the plan records that it is heuristic.

limitations: The opt-in is per task and per language. An unidentified file is text, not unsupported. The symbol tool filters by the recorded tier, so promotion from C to B is a deliberate act (PX-028). The desktop Review screen does not show the language line yet.
